subject: Security walkthrough + MAP checkpoints for BlueHarbor evaluation
messages:
From: Anita Shah <anita@blueharbor.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@blueharbor.com>, security@blueharbor.com
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP + security gating questions ahead of procurement review

Hi Naomi / Ben —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement wants a short mutual action plan focused on security gates so we can present to the committee on Jan 12. High level asks from our side: SOC 2 evidence (recent report + control matrix), completed SIG/CAIQ, DPA with data residency/retention language, and clarification on how deletion / export works for EU workloads.

Can you share a suggested MAP with owners, acceptance criteria and realistic turnaround times? Also attaching the buyer-side SIG spreadsheet with a couple of follow-up questions (attached: buyer_sig_questionnaire.xlsx).

We'd like the MAP to show (1) when we can expect SOC 2 artifacts, (2) a date for returning the CAIQ, (3) DPA redline cadence, and (4) data retention options and API/controls for deletion.

Short on time — can you get a draft to me by end of next week?

Thanks,
Anita
Anita Shah
Senior Procurement Manager
BlueHarbor Analytics

Attachment: buyer_sig_questionnaire.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 10:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MAP + security gating questions ahead of procurement review

Anita — thanks, this is clear. Attached is a working MAP draft (map-draft-v1.xlsx) and a one-page acceptance summary below. I tried to balance your committee's timeline with realistic engineering / legal turnaround.

Proposed MAP checkpoints (owners + target windows):

1) SOC 2 - Evidence & scope (owner: Security Ops / Naomi)
   - Deliverables: SOC 2 Type II report (last 12 months) + control matrix (CSV) + list of in-scope endpoints
   - Target: initial delivery within 3 business days of request (we have the 2026 report ready)
   - Acceptance criteria: report + matrix uploaded to shared drive and confirmation from BlueHarbor security team

2) SIG/CAIQ questionnaire (owner: Security Ops / Marcus)
   - Deliverables: completed .pdf and answers tracked in your spreadsheet
   - Target: returned within 5 business days; clarifying Qs back-and-forth absorbed into acceptance window (up to 2 business days)
   - Acceptance criteria: CAIQ marked as "answered" and outstanding items logged as low/medium/high risk

3) DPA redlines and legal review (owner: Legal / Kimberly)
   - Deliverables: annotated DPA, proposed carveouts, auditable signature path
   - Target: initial redline review 2 business days; final DocuSign route scheduled after commercial sign-off
   - Acceptance criteria: DPA countersigned or execution plan agreed (DocuSign envelope link provided below)

4) Data retention / residency options (owner: Product & Engineering / Marcus)
   - Deliverables: spec doc for retention windows (default 30 days), optional 12-month retention for contract customers, EU region residency option, deletion API description, export runbook
   - Target: spec + API docs within 4 business days; demo of deletion/export in staging within 7 business days
   - Acceptance criteria: BlueHarbor validates deletion behavior in staging; retention window codified in DPA annex

5) SLA / Escalation & fallback (owner: Customer Success / Ben)
   - Deliverables: proposed SLA uplifts, on-call escalation path, temporary workarounds (read-only fallback variant)
   - Target: propose SLA uplift options within 2 business days

Escalation & tie-breakers:
- If DPA redlines introduce commercial impact, Naomi will schedule an exec alignment call (CS + Sales + Legal) within 24 hours.
- If SOC2 evidence raises scope questions, Marcus will host a 30-min technical walkthrough within 48 hours.

Notes on sensitive items:
- KMS options: customer-managed keys available via KMS/HSM (requires DMZ config; lead time 2–3 weeks for on-prem CMEK).
- Data residency: EU-hosted inference available in our EU region; keys and audit logs remain under customer control via KMS integration.

Attachments included: map-draft-v1.xlsx, soc2-report-2026.pdf, sig-caiq-response.pdf (stubs).

If this looks good I can push a clean MAP and a one-pager for procurement. Happy to hop on a quick call Wednesday to walk through.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: map-draft-v1.xlsx, soc2-report-2026.pdf, sig-caiq-response.pdf (stubs)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Anita — appreciate the clear ask. Naomi — looks great. Two quick operational notes from Sales:

- We can offer a limited "canary" demo within an EU region tenant next week (Dec 28–30) so your procurement/security folks can exercise the delete/export flow before the Jan 12 committee.
- I'll block 45 mins with Tom + your procurement team for Jan 6 to review the MAP and the DPA carveouts (calendar invite to follow).

If BlueHarbor wants tighter SLA guarantees for the evaluation window, we can agree on a short-term uplift (30-day trial SLA) — happy to propose numbers once procurement signals priority.

—Ben

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Anita / team — quick legal note on the DPA:

- We generally accept standard customer redlines for retention and deletion, but request (1) an auditable export window and (2) a 30-day hold for legal preservation if a specific subpoena/incident is outstanding. We can carve that to a 7-day shorter hold on enterprise plans by mutual agreement.
- For SIG exceptions: please flag any "requires mitigation" controls separately; we will accept compensating controls where appropriate.
- If BlueHarbor needs an escrow / custom keystore clause, we'll prepare an addendum and estimate delivery time (typically 2–3 weeks for custom legal + engineering work).

I'll prepare the annotated DPA redline and send via DocuSign for your review. If procurement wants faster routing, please confirm the signers.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
